subject: MAP: Deployment performance benchmarking & close timeline — Starlite AI
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: MAP: Draft benchmarking plan & timeline

Hi Anita —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, we put together a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the performance evaluation you requested so we can align on a recommended deployment option (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and close timeline. Attached is a working MAP (see Starlite_MAP_v2.xlsx) — the benchmarking page is a prioritized checklist: measurements, owners, and target dates.

Key asks from your side:
- Give us a representative prompt set (10–20 sequences) and expected concurrency patterns (typical vs peak).
- Confirm whether tests can run against production traffic mirroring or if we should use synthetic load (recommended: production-like replay).

Our proposed measurement plan (short):
- Metrics: TTFT (time to first token), p50/p95 generation latency per token, end-to-end throughput (tokens/sec), sustained concurrency profiles, and autoscale reaction times.
- Environments: Hosted (multi-tenant), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), Private (VPC/on-prem).
- Scenarios: cold start, warm KV-cache, noisy-neighbor stress, and sustained 1-hour load at peak concurrency.

Target milestones:
- Benchmark execution: by 2026-02-23
- MAP sign-off and procurement kickoff: by 2026-03-05
- Production rollout window: 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-17

I tagged Neha and Marcus on the MAP — Marcus will run the measurement harness, Neha will own procurement questions and commercial framing. Let me know if those dates work and whether procurement should be looped now or after we share results.

Best,
Jordan

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-21T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Benchmark plan + owners (Starlite)

Team — quick plan so we can hit Anita's ask by 02/23. Replied to the customer to loop procurement.

Scope (Marcus): run the measurement harness against three deployments: Hosted (prod endpoint), Dedicated (reserved pool sim), Private (staging VPC replay). Capture: TTFT, p50/p95 token latency, end-to-end throughput (tokens/sec), sustained concurrency (1,5,10,25 concurrent sessions), autoscale up/down times, and CPU/GPU utilization traces. Include variability analysis (stddev, coefficient of variation) for each metric.

Test specifics:
- Workloads: 15-sequence prompt set (Anita to provide).
- Cache conditions: cold start and warm (KV cache primed with typical session history).
- Noisy-neighbor: run 30-minute background synthetic jobs on Hosted to measure isolation.
- Autoscale: step up load and capture time to provision extra GPUs and time to return to baseline.

Deliverables (Marcus): CSV with per-trial metrics + short narrative (example: "Hosted p95 spike under noisy load; Dedicated stable at Xms; Private consistent but provisioning latency Ys"). Attach sample logs.

Neha: prepare short commercial notes for each option (cost delta, commit terms). Laura: FYI for escalation path / SLA language.

Thanks — Jordan
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-23T17:06:00-08:00
Subject: Results: Starlite benchmarking run (attached)

Team — attached are the raw CSV and a short log extract. High-level summary here (all numbers median over 5 runs unless noted):

Attached: benchmark_results_20260223.csv, inference_logs_sample.txt

Key metrics (representative):
- Hosted (multi-tenant prod endpoint):
  - TTFT (p50/p95): 240ms / 480ms
  - Generation p50/p95 (per token): 10ms / 45ms
  - Throughput (tokens/sec sustained, 8 concurrent): 650 t/s
  - Concurrency stress (25 sessions): p95 latency increased to ~1.2s; CV (latency) = 0.42
  - Autoscale: scales up in ~65s under sustained spike; scale-down ~300s
  - Notes: observable latency spikes under noisy-neighbor background jobs; no evidence of request loss.

- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, same instance types):
  - TTFT (p50/p95): 190ms / 220ms
  - Generation p50/p95 (per token): 8ms / 12ms
  - Throughput (tokens/sec sustained, 8 concurrent): 1,050 t/s
  - Concurrency stress (25 sessions): p95 latency ~260ms; CV = 0.08
  - Autoscale: instant headroom inside pool; when exhausted, adding extra reserved nodes ~95s
  - Notes: very predictable latency and throughput; isolation eliminates noisy-neighbor variance.

- Private (staging VPC, customer-managed infra parity):
  - TTFT (p50/p95): 205ms / 230ms
  - Generation p50/p95 (per token): 9ms / 15ms
  - Throughput (tokens/sec sustained, 8 concurrent): 980 t/s
  - Concurrency stress (25 sessions): p95 latency ~300ms; CV = 0.12
  - Autoscale: depends on customer's infra (in staging we saw ~140s to provision extra capacity via our on-prem agent)
  - Notes: performance largely consistent; provisioning latency depends on customer's VM provisioning and network link.

Interpretation:
- Dedicated gives the best predictability and throughput for Starlite's peak workloads.
- Hosted is lowest-friction (fastest to start) but exposed to higher latency variance under noisy neighbors and has slower autoscale reaction for large spikes.
- Private matches Dedicated performance when infra is right-sized but introduces procurement/ops overhead and slower provisioning in our staging tests.

I'll attach the CSV with trial-level numbers and the log excerpt showing p95 jump events on Hosted during noisy-neighbor test.

— Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita@starliteai.com>, procurement@starliteai.com

Date: 2026-02-24T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Starlite benchmarking: summary, recommendation, and MAP updates

Hi Anita / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the replay data. We completed the benchmarking runs and attached the MAP (Starlite_MAP_v2.xlsx) and the results CSV for your review. TL;DR: Dedicated is the recommended default for Starlite if predictability and latency SLOs are the priority; Hosted is recommended for rapid MVP rollout if you prefer minimal ops; Private is an option if you require network isolation or specific compliance controls, but expect longer provisioning times and additional ops coordination.

Summary of tradeoffs (short):
- Hosted: fastest time-to-value, easier updates and streaming support; p95 spikes under noisy neighbors and slower autoscale (65s to add capacity in our tests). Good for early releases where commit/ops friction is a blocker.
- Dedicated: best throughput and predictability; p95 stays low even at high concurrency. Slightly higher committed cost but better unit economics at scale.
- Private: comparable to Dedicated if infra is well-configured; provisioning depends on your VM/cluster orchestration and network — we saw ~140s provisioning time in staging. Good for compliance-sensitive deployments.

Recommended MAP updates and close timeline:
- 2026-02-24: Share results + updated MAP (done).
- 2026-03-02: Procurement Q&A finalized (Neha to lead).
- 2026-03-05: MAP sign-off and PO (target close).
- 2026-03-10 — 2026-03-17: Provisioned deployment and smoke verification.

Next steps I propose:
1) Procurement kickoff — Neha will share pricing scenarios for Dedicated vs Private (commit terms and lead times).
2) If you want a low-friction start, we can spin a Hosted sandbox and cutover to Dedicated after PO.
3) If Private is required, we'll schedule the VPN window and a runbook for provisioning.

Anita — does that timeline work? If so, I'll schedule the procurement call next week and share a short canary plan for the first week of production.

Best,
Jordan
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
